answer: Persistent transcript auction. Each identity must maintain a public, append-only replay of its recent interactions; peers randomly challenge segments, and failure to answer from the live log within a tight window voids standing. Since attention leaves a verifiable echo across time, clones must fund continuous re-answering at every terrace of the challenge tree, not one-time registration. Reaching a summit of trust requires months of unbroken history, so an attacker pays parallel sustained compute and monitoring per identity.
